topic: Substance misuse screening in mental health patients
usual_baseline: About half to two-thirds of patients are asked about substance use: 69% [3115], 7/12 [3333], nearly half not asked [3238]. Older people, women and ward referrals are asked least (over 80s 0%) [3115]. Drug screening was documented in 57.5% and offered to 52.5% [3473]. Specialist service involvement is weakest (62.06% on admission, 42.8% at discharge) [3514].
fix_that_works: A training session on results and NICE recommendations raised screening from 69% to 93%, over 80s from 0% to 60% and ward referrals from 33.3% to 85% [3115]. At re-audit, 78% were asked about alcohol and 77% about drugs, with documented advice up 21% [3238].
fix_that_fails: No intervention was followed by no improvement. Items that stayed poor: at re-audit, 27% with identified misuse had no intervention documented [3238]. Over 80s reached only 60% after training [3115].
consultant_advice: Asking the question is easy to improve with teaching. The gap lies in what happens next: advice, brief intervention and specialist referral, and reasons for refused drug tests [3473]. Audit the action taken for positive screens, and include older patients and women.
